s:
Which of the principles are common for Bhakti and Sufi movement ?

I. Monotheism

II. Asceticism

III. Religious tolerance

IV. Accepted the idol worship to some extent
x: Monotheism, asceticism and religious tolerance were common to both; idol worship was not accepted by the Sufis or by the nirguna Bhakti saints, so IV is wrong.

s: The philosophy of Sufism is similar to the Hindu philosophy of
x: Sufism, like Bhakti, stressed loving devotion to one God over formal ritual, so its philosophy parallels Bhakti (devotion), not karma, kalpa or gyana.

s: A common feature to all Bhakti Saints was that they
o: composed their verses in the languages understood by their followers.
rejected the authority of the priestly class.
encouraged women to go to the temples.
x: All Bhakti saints composed verses in the languages of their followers. Rejecting priests, idol worship and sending women to temples were not shared by all.

s: Hindustani music was largely influenced by:
x: Hindustani music was shaped largely by the Arabo-Persian music brought by Muslim rulers and Sufi musicians; European music had no such role.

s: The followers of Gorakhnath were called
x:
Most books and keys: Jogis. Strictly: they are also called Nath-panthis (NextGen IH Part 5 p.8: 'Nath followers of Gorakhnath'), so option b is not wrong either.

s:
With reference of Hath Yog, which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Hath Yog was practiced by Nathpanthis.

II. Hath Yog technique was also adopted by the Sufis.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Both are correct: Hath Yoga was the practice of the Nathpanthis (Gorakhnath, Matsyendranath), and its techniques, through the Amritakund, were adopted by the Sufis.

s: Who among the following is founder of Satnami sect?
x: Guru Ghasidas founded the Satnami panth of Chhattisgarh (c. 1820s); Ravidas, Ramdas and Tukaram were other saints. An earlier Satnami sect had begun at Narnaul in 1657.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
s: In which city did the Prime Minister attend the 350th birth anniversary of Guru Gobind Singh in 2017?
x: PM Modi attended the 350th birth anniversary (Prakash Parv) celebrations of Guru Gobind Singh at Patna – his birthplace – on 5 January 2017 and released a stamp. Nanded is where the Guru died; Anandpur is where he founded the Khalsa.

s: Which Sikh Guru was born in Patna?
x: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, was born at Patna in 1666 (Takht Sri Patna Sahib). Nanak was born at Talwandi and Tegh Bahadur at Amritsar.

s: Who was the tenth (10th) Guru of the Sikhs?
x: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and last Guru; he founded the Khalsa in 1699. Tegh Bahadur was the 9th, Har Kishan the 8th, and Banda Bahadur was his disciple, not a Guru.

s: Under which Sikh Guru, the Sikhs were transformed into the 'Khalsa'?
x: Guru Gobind Singh transformed the Sikhs into the Khalsa on Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur. Tegh Bahadur, Arjun and Nanak came before the Khalsa.

s: Guru Gobind Singh’s greatness lies in the fact that :
o: He formed the military order of Sikhs
He was the founder of Sikh state
x: Guru Gobind Singh's greatness lies in turning the Sikhs into a military order, the Khalsa. The first Sikh state was set up by Banda Bahadur (1710), and he did not defeat Aurangzeb.

s: In which year did Guru Govind Singh found ‘Khalsa’?
x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on Baisakhi, 13 April 1699, at Anandpur. 1707 is Aurangzeb's death and 1599 / 1789 have no link.

s: Guru Gobind Singh greatness lies in the fact that
o: he formed the military order of Sikh.
he was the founder of Sikh state.
x: Guru Gobind Singh made the Sikhs a military order through the Khalsa (Singh/Kaur surnames, Five Ks). The Sikh state was founded by Banda Bahadur (1710), and he did not defeat Aurangzeb.

s: How many years ago Khalsa Panth started?
x: The Khalsa Panth was founded in 1699, so in 2000 (the exam year) it was about 300 years old (its tercentenary was celebrated in 1999).

s: The Guru who founded the ‘Khalsa’ was :
x: The Khalsa was founded by the tenth Guru, Gobind Singh, in 1699. Har Rai, Har Kishan and Tegh Bahadur preceded him.

s: Which among the following Sikh Gurus instituted the Khalsa Panth?
x: Guru Gobind Singh instituted the Khalsa Panth on Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur (Keshgarh Sahib). Tegh Bahadur, Arjan Dev and Nanak came earlier.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
s: Which of the following cities was the capital of Maharaja Ranjit Singh?
x: Ranjit Singh captured Lahore in 1799 and made it the capital of his kingdom; Amritsar was its religious capital.

s: Capital of Kingdom of Maharaja Ranjit Singh was:
x: Lahore, taken in 1799, was the capital of Ranjit Singh's kingdom. Amritsar was its religious centre; Patiala and Kapurthala were separate Sikh states.

s: Who among the following has said, ‘God intended me to look upon all religions with one eye, that is why he took away the light from the other’?
x: Maharaja Ranjit Singh, blind in one eye from smallpox, said God meant him to look on all religions with one eye. He was a tolerant ruler with Hindu and Muslim ministers.

s: To which Misl did Ranjeet Singh belong:
x: Ranjit Singh was the son of Maha (Mahan) Singh, chief of the Sukerchakia misl. Sandhawalia, Ahluwalia and Ramgarhia were other Sikh families/misls.

s: Maharaja Ranjit Singh made his political and religious capital to
x: Ranjit Singh took Lahore in 1799 (political capital) and Amritsar later (religious capital, Golden Temple). So 'Lahore, Amritsar' fits; Patiala and Kapurthala were never his capitals.

s: Who has conferred the title of ‘Raja’ to Ranjit Singh?
x: In 1799 the Afghan ruler Zaman Shah, whose cannons Ranjit Singh had recovered from the Jhelum, appointed him governor of Lahore with the title of Raja. Nadir Shah died in 1747, long before Ranjit Singh's rise.

s: Ranjit Singh was related to which Misl?
x: Ranjit Singh's father Maha Singh was chief of the Sukerchakia misl, and Ranjit Singh belonged to it; Singhpuria, Ahluwalia and Ramgarhia were other misls.

s: Which of the following was included in the Maharaja Ranjit Singh empire?
x: Ranjit Singh conquered Kashmir (Srinagar) in 1819, so it lay in his empire. Delhi stayed with the Mughals/British, Kabul with the Afghans, and Makrana is in Rajasthan.

s: The Sikh Guru executed by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb was
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, was executed on Aurangzeb's orders at Delhi in 1675. Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir (1606); Gobind Singh died at Nanded in 1708.

s: Aurangzeb is responsible for which Sikh prophet’s death?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, was executed on Aurangzeb's orders at Delhi in 1675. Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir (1606); Gobind Singh died at Nanded in 1708.

s: Who was the Sikh Guru to be slaughtered by Aurangzeb?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, was executed on Aurangzeb's orders at Delhi in 1675. Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir (1606); Gobind Singh died at Nanded in 1708.

s: Which Sikh Guru was publicly killed by Aurangzeb in 1675 for not embracing Islam?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was publicly executed at Chandni Chowk, Delhi, in 1675 on Aurangzeb's orders for refusing to embrace Islam. Arjun Dev died under Jahangir in 1606.

s:
Which of the following Sikh Gurus were penalised with death by the Rulers of the time?

I. Guru Angad

II. Guru Arjan Dev

III. Guru Har Gobind

IV. Guru Tegh Bahadur
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
x: Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir (1606) and Tegh Bahadur under Aurangzeb (1675) – the two martyred Gurus. Hargobind was only imprisoned at Gwalior and freed; Angad was not executed.

s: To which Sikh Guru, Akbar donated 500 Bighas of land?
x: Akbar granted about 500 bighas of land to the fourth Guru, Ram Das, where Ramdaspur (Amritsar) and its tank grew. Arjan Dev later built the Harmandir; Har Rai and Tegh Bahadur came after Akbar.

s: Who was the last King of Sikh empire?
x: Maharaja Duleep Singh, Ranjit Singh's youngest son, was the last king of the Sikh empire (1843-1849); Punjab was annexed in 1849. Kharak Singh, Nau Nihal Singh and Sher Singh ruled before him.

s: Who was last king of Sikh empire?
x: Maharaja Duleep Singh, Ranjit Singh's youngest son, was the last king of the Sikh empire (1843-1849); Punjab was annexed in 1849. Kharak Singh, Nau Nihal Singh and Sher Singh ruled before him.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct about Dalip Singh, the ex-Maharaja of Punjab?
o: He died in Paris on 23 October, 1893
He never renounced the Sikh faith
x:
Most books and keys: (a) 'died in Paris on 23 October 1893'. Strictly: most references give 22 October 1893 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duleep_Singh lead; its Death section, citing Khushwant Singh, gives 23 October).
Duleep Singh died in a Paris hotel in October 1893, so (a) is the only acceptable statement. He was buried with Christian rites at Elveden, England (not cremated at Nasik); he had converted to Christianity in 1853 before returning to Sikhism in 1886, and he went to Russia in 1887 to seek Tsar Alexander III's help.

s: The successor of Maharaja Ranjit Singh was :
x: After Ranjit Singh died in June 1839, his eldest son Kharak (Khadag) Singh succeeded him; Nau Nihal Singh and Sher Singh followed. Hari Singh Nalwa was his general, not a successor.

s: Who was the successor of Maharaja Ranjit Singh?
x: After Ranjit Singh died in June 1839, his eldest son Kharak (Khadag) Singh succeeded him; Nau Nihal Singh and Sher Singh followed. Hari Singh Nalwa was his general, not a successor.

s: Which of the following statement about the last ruler of Punjab is correct?
o: He died in Paris on 23rd October, 1893.
He last ritual was performed in Nasik.
He never apostated the Sikh religion.
x:
Most books and keys: (a) 'died in Paris on 23 October 1893'. Strictly: most references give 22 October 1893 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duleep_Singh lead; its Death section, citing Khushwant Singh, gives 23 October).
Duleep Singh died in a Paris hotel in October 1893, so (a) is the only acceptable statement. He was buried with Christian rites at Elveden, England (not cremated at Nasik); he had converted to Christianity in 1853 before returning to Sikhism in 1886, and he went to Russia in 1887 to seek Tsar Alexander III's help.

s: The word 'Sikh' means
x: 'Sikh' comes from the Sanskrit shishya – a disciple or learner of the Guru. 'Khalsa' means pure; soldier, monk and devotee are not the word's meaning.

s: Which of the following was the birthplace of Guru Nanak?
x: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Talwandi, now Nankana Sahib (Pakistan). Amritsar was founded by Guru Ram Das and Nanded is linked to Guru Gobind Singh.

s: Who was the successor of Guru Nanak?
x: Guru Nanak chose Bhai Lehna, who became Guru Angad, as his successor before his death in 1539. Amar Das (3rd), Ram Das (4th), Arjan (5th) and Hargobind (6th) came later.

s: Who had Guru Nanak appointed his successor?
x: Guru Nanak appointed Bhai Lehna, who became Guru Angad, as his successor. Amar Das and Ram Das were the 3rd and 4th Gurus; Har Rai the 7th.

x: Guru Ram Das founded Amritsar and began the tank; his successor Guru Arjun Dev completed the Harmandir Sahib (1604) and installed the Adi Granth there.

s: The city of Amritsar in Punjab was established by:
x: Amritsar (first called Ramdaspur) was founded by the fourth Guru, Ram Das, on land granted by Akbar. Nanak, Tegh Bahadur and Gobind Singh are linked to Talwandi, Anandpur and Patna.

s: Nanded is considered sacred by Sikhs due to whose Mausoleum?
x: Takht Sri Hazur Sahib at Nanded (Maharashtra) marks the death and cremation of Guru Gobind Singh (1708). Amar Das, Angad and Arjun Dev are linked to Punjab.

s: The original name of Banda Bahadur was –
x: Banda Singh Bahadur was originally named Lachhman Dev; the name 'Banda' was given to him by Guru Gobind Singh at Nanded (1708).

s: Who painted the famous ‘Mona Lisa’?
x: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci (c. 1503-19), not by Michelangelo, Reynolds or Rembrandt.

s: Alexander Kerensky was

a close confident of Lenin, with whose help the Czar was dethroned.
the head of the Czar’s army.
x: Alexander Kerensky headed the Russian Provisional Government from July 1917 until the Bolsheviks seized power in the October Revolution; he was Lenin's opponent, not his confidant.

s: Who was the father of ‘Russian Revolution?’
x: V.I. Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and is called its father; Stalin, Khrushchev and Brezhnev were later Soviet leaders.

s: In 1911 Revolution of China resulted in
x: The 1911 (Xinhai) Revolution overthrew the Qing dynasty and set up the Republic of China (1912).

s: The Crimean War in 1854-56 was fought between
x: The Crimean War (1853-56) was fought between Russia and the Ottoman Empire (Turkey); Britain, France and Sardinia joined on Turkey's side.

s: In which country did the first Marxist Revolution took place?
x: The first Marxist revolution was the Bolshevik (October) Revolution of 1917 in Russia.

s: The provisional goverment of 1917 in Russia was headed by
x:
Most books and keys: Alexander Kerensky. Strictly, Prince Lvov headed the Provisional Government first (March-July 1917) and Kerensky from July 1917 (general knowledge, not checked).
The Provisional Government of 1917 is linked with Alexander Kerensky, who headed it from July 1917 until the October Revolution; its first head (March-July 1917) was Prince Georgy Lvov.

s:
Due to which of the following factors, the Industrial Revolution took place in England in the eighteenth century?

I. The discovery of coal and iron deposits.

II. The discovery of steam power.

III. the introduction of railways.

IV. The regular supply of raw materials.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x:
Most keys: I, II, III and IV. Strictly, railways (1825-30) were a later development, not a cause of the 18th-century start (general knowledge).
The answer keys give all four: coal and iron, steam power, the railways and a regular supply of raw materials. Railways (from 1825) came after the 18th-century start and really sustained the revolution.

s:
Which among the following was/were among the factors for England to experience the Industrial Revolution first?

I. The scientific inventions had paved the way for Industrial Revolution.

II. It had favourable social and political structures in place.

III. Navigable rivers had made inland transport easier.

IV. It had seen the ascendancy of capitalist practices.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: All four helped England industrialise first: scientific inventions, favourable social and political structures, navigable rivers for inland transport, and the rise of capitalist practices.

s:
Arrange the following inventions in the field of cotton Industry in chronological order (starting with the earliest).

I. James Hargreaves’s Spinning Jenny

II. John Kay’s Flying Shuttle

III. Samuel Crompton’s Mule

IV. Richard Arkwright’s Water Frame
Codes
x: Kay's flying shuttle (1733), Hargreaves's spinning jenny (1764), Arkwright's water frame (1769) and Crompton's mule (1779) - II, I, IV, III.

s:
Industrial Revolution in Europe emerged due to

I. locating the production process in the countryside.

II. declining of the guilds because of non farming production coming under the single roof (the factory).

III. Growing role of Merchant capitalists in the production process.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The factory brought non-farm production under one roof and undermined the guilds, and merchant capitalists gained a growing role (II and III). Industrial production moved into town factories, so I is wrong.

s: When was the ‘Boxer Rebellion’ happened in China?
x: The Boxer Rebellion, an anti-foreign uprising in China (1899-1901), peaked in 1900 with the siege of the Beijing legations.

s:
Consider the following statements concerning the Russian Revolution.

I. The Bolsheviks believed that in a repressive society like Tsarist Russia, the party should be disciplined and should control the number of its members.

II. The Mensheviks believed that the party should be opened to all (as in Germany).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Lenin's Bolsheviks wanted a small, disciplined party in Tsarist Russia; the Mensheviks wanted a party open to all, as in Germany. Both statements are correct.

s: The first ancient Civilisation to develop the art of writing in a proper system was
x: The Sumerians of Mesopotamia developed cuneiform, the first proper system of writing (c. 3200 BC), before Egyptian hieroglyphs; the Indus script is undeciphered.

s:
Which, among the following, is/are the impact/impacts of industrial revolution in England?

I. Cottage industry was replaced by the factory system of production using machines.

II. It led to the overpopulation of villages.

III. It led to the emergence of working class movements.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The Industrial Revolution replaced cottage industry with the factory system and gave rise to working-class movements (I and III); migration crowded the towns, not the villages, so II is wrong.

s:
Statement I The passing of the coercive acts mandate reconciliation between Britain and her American colonies virtually impossible. Statement II The British parliament, having issued the Stamp Act in 1765, repealed it later.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both the statements are individually true, but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
x: Both are true: the Coercive Acts (1774) made reconciliation virtually impossible, and the Stamp Act of 1765 was repealed in 1766. The repeal came earlier and does not explain the Coercive Acts, so II is not the explanation of I.

s: The first Emperor of France was
x: Napoleon Bonaparte became Emperor of the French in 1804, the first emperor of France; Charlemagne was emperor of the Romans (800), and Louis XIV a king.

s: When did the Stamp Act Congress consisting of delegates from 9 of the 13 colonies of America meet in New York City?
x: The Stamp Act Congress of delegates from 9 of the 13 colonies met in New York City in October 1765 to protest the Stamp Act.

s: The Treaty of Schonbrunn (1809) was signed after which of the following battles?
x: The Treaty of Schonbrunn (October 1809) followed Napoleon's victory over Austria at Wagram; Austerlitz led to Pressburg (1805) and Tilsit was a treaty (1807), not a battle.

s: Which among the following statements is not correct about the ‘Reign of Terror’?
o: The Jacobins dashed out the Girondists with the help of Sans-Culottes.
The Jacobins were in league with the French clergy.
The arrest for anti-revolutionary activities was by law restricted to the political class.
The Reign of Terror came to an end with the execution of Robespierre by guillotine in July, 1794.
x:
Most keys: (c) - arrests were not restricted to the political class. Strictly, (b) is also untrue: the Jacobins were anti-clerical, not in league with the clergy.
Not correct: the Law of Suspects (1793) allowed anyone, not only the political class, to be arrested. The Jacobins and sans-culottes did purge the Girondins (June 1793), and the Terror ended with Robespierre's execution in July 1794.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Olympe de Gouges (1748- 1793) is correct?
o: She declared that although citizens should have equal rights, they are not entitled to the same honours by the State.
She was a supporter of the Jacobin government.
She was jailed for treason by the National Assembly.
She declared that the nation is the union of woman and man.
x: Olympe de Gouges, author of the Declaration of the Rights of Woman (1791), wrote that the nation is the union of woman and man. She opposed the Jacobins and was guillotined in 1793; she claimed equal honours for women too.

s: With which one of the following is the Tennis Court Oath associated?
x: The Tennis Court Oath (20 June 1789) was sworn by the Third Estate deputies of the National Assembly at Versailles, at the start of the French Revolution.

s: Which one of the following combinations of year and event concerning the French Revolution is correctly matched?
x: The National Convention met in September 1792 and abolished the monarchy; the Tennis Court Oath was 1789 and the Napoleonic Code 1804.

s: The Stamp Act Congress consisting of delegates from nine of thirteen colonies met in 1765 at
x: The Stamp Act Congress met in New York City in October 1765; Philadelphia hosted the later Continental Congresses.

s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true for Olympe de Gouges?

I. She was one of the most important politically active woman in revolutionary frame.

II. She was one of the members of the committee that drafted the declaration of rights of man and citizen.

III. She wrote the declaration of the rights of woman and citizen.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Olympe de Gouges was a politically active woman of the Revolution and wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen (1791); she was not on the committee that drafted the Rights of Man (1789).

s:
Which of the following was/were among the decisions taken by the first continental Congress held in Philadelphia in September, 1774?

I. It rejected a plan for a colonial union under the British authority.

II. It drew up a statement of grievances.

III. It agreed upon a scheme to stop trade between the colonies and England.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The First Continental Congress (Philadelphia, 1774) rejected Galloway's plan of union under British authority, drew up a statement of grievances and agreed the Continental Association to stop trade with England - all three.

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the American Revolution is/are correct?

I. The American Revolution was a conflict between British settlers and native Americans.

II. The Americans refused to pay taxes imposed by the British Parliament in which the Americans had no representation.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The American Revolution was a conflict between the colonists and Britain over taxes voted by a Parliament where they had no representation; it was not settlers against Native Americans. Only II is correct.

s:
Consider the following statements concerning the American war of Independence.

I. The Americans raised the slogan, “No taxation without representation.”

II. The American merchants resorted to boycott the British products.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The colonists raised 'No taxation without representation' and American merchants boycotted British goods. Both are correct.

s: Which country among the following was not a part of the Third Coalition against Napoleon?
x: The Third Coalition (1805) of Britain, Austria, Russia and Sweden was formed against France; France was the enemy, not a member.

s: What were the taxes extracted by Church during late eighteenth century in the French Society called?
x: The tithe was the tax (about one-tenth of produce) that the Church collected in pre-revolutionary France. The taille was a direct tax paid to the state, the livre was the currency, and jizya was a Muslim poll tax.

s: The earliest Europeans to land on Indian soil re were the

s: Who among the following Europeans were the last to come to pre-independence India as traders?
x: The French were the last Europeans to come to India as traders: their company was founded in 1664 and their first factory set up at Surat in 1668, after the Portuguese, Dutch and English.

x: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to come to India for trade, with Vasco da Gama's arrival at Calicut in 1498.

s:

2. The Dutch
3. The French
4. The Portuguese

Code:

s:

s: Who discovered "The Cape of Good Hope"?
x: Bartholomew Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1487-88 (he called it the Cape of Storms); Vasco da Gama used his route ten years later.

s: What is the correct North-South sequence of the following civilisations?
x: From north to south: Aztec (central Mexico), Maya (southern Mexico and Central America), Muisca (Colombia), Inca (Peru) - Aztec-Maya-Muisca-Inca.

s: Who was the first to circumnavigate the earth?
x: Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish expedition (1519-22) made the first circumnavigation of the earth; Magellan was killed in the Philippines and Elcano completed it. Cook and Amundsen came much later.

x: Columbus (1492) reached the Americas while seeking a western route to India; India's sea route was found by Vasco da Gama in 1498. Moved to history.

x: Jahangir gave the title 'English Khan' to Captain William Hawkins (court 1609-11), who conversed with him in Turki; not to Roe, Terry or the Portuguese governors.

s: Who among the following is the envoy of British King James-I sent to Jahangir’s Court?
x: William Hawkins brought King James I's letter to Jahangir's court (1609); Finch was a merchant with him, Della Valle an Italian traveller and Terry Roe's chaplain.

s: Whom of the following Englishman was given the title of English Khan by Jahangir?
x: Jahangir gave the title 'English Khan' to Captain William Hawkins (court 1609-11), who conversed with him in Turki; not to Roe, Terry or the Portuguese governors.

s: Which among the following foreign travellers had described that Mughal Emperors used to drink water brought from River Ganga in Bronze Vessels?
x: Edward Terry, Roe's chaplain at Jahangir's court (1616-19), described in his 'Voyage to East-India' how the emperor's drinking water was brought from the Ganga; the UPPSC key gives Terry.

s:
With reference to the Captain Hawkins, which of the following statements is correct?
(1) He came to India in 1611 as an envoy of James-I.
(2) He was very well versed in Turkish language.
x: Only (2): Hawkins knew Turki well and spoke with Jahangir without an interpreter. (1) is wrong: he reached Surat in 1608 and the court in 1609; 1611 is when he left.

s: Bombay acquired by the English originally belonged to the
x: Bombay belonged to the Portuguese; it came to Charles II as the dowry of Catherine of Braganza (1661-62) and was given to the Company in 1668.

s: Which one of the following European trading company was the first to establish its factory at Surat?
x: The English were the first European company to set up a factory at Surat (1613, Jahangir's permission); the Dutch came there in 1616 and the French in 1668.

s: Where in India did Britishers set up their first factory in 1613?
x: The English set up their first (permanent) factory at Surat in 1613, after Captain Best's victory over the Portuguese at Swally.

s: Masulipatnam, a settlement founded in 1611 by the English, acted as their headquarters until they finally moved to Madras in ____.
x: The English settlement at Masulipatnam (1611) was their headquarters until they moved to Madras in 1641.

s:
With reference to Indian history, consider the following statements:

A. The Dutch established their factories/warehouses on the east coast on lands granted to them by Gajapati rulers.

B. Alfonso de Albuquerque captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate.

C. The English East India Company established a factory at Madras on a plot of land leased from a representative of the Vijayanagara empire.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: B and C only. Albuquerque took Goa from Bijapur (1510), and the English got Madras (1639) from the Chandragiri ruler, a representative of Vijayanagara. A is wrong: the Dutch got their east-coast lands from Golconda and Vijayanagara rulers; the Gajapatis had ended in the 16th century.

s: With reference to the entry of European powers into India, which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: The English opened their first factory in South India at Masulipattam
In Eastern India, the English Company opened its first factory in Orissa in 1633
Under the leadership of Dupleix, the French occupied Madras in 1746
x: Not correct: the Portuguese captured Goa in 1510 (Albuquerque, from Bijapur), not 1499. The English did open their first southern factory at Masulipatnam and their first eastern one in Orissa (1633), and the French under Dupleix took Madras in 1746.

o: The English opened their first factory in South India

Under the leadership of Dupleix, the French occupied
x: Not correct: the Portuguese captured Goa in 1510 (Albuquerque, from Bijapur), not 1499. The English did open their first southern factory at Masulipatnam and their first eastern one in Orissa (1633), and the French under Dupleix took Madras in 1746.

s: The first to start a joint stock company to trade with India were :
x: Of the options the Dutch were first: the VOC (1602), formed by merging companies, was a joint-stock company. The English EIC (1600) was earlier but is not among the options.

s: Blue Water Policy is associated with

s: Who among the following introduced the Blue Water Policy?
x: The Blue Water Policy, naval mastery of the Indian Ocean, was introduced by the first Viceroy Francisco de Almeida; Albuquerque turned to territorial conquest.

s: Who was the real founder of Portuguese power in India?
x: Albuquerque (1509-15) is the real founder of Portuguese power in India: he took Goa from Bijapur (1510) and controlled the entrances to the Indian Ocean. Almeida was the first Viceroy and da Gama the discoverer.

s: Who is considered as the real founder of the Portuguese power in India?
x: Albuquerque (1509-15) is the real founder of Portuguese power in India: he took Goa from Bijapur (1510) and controlled the entrances to the Indian Ocean. Almeida was the first Viceroy and da Gama the discoverer.

s: Who was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India?
x: Francisco de Almeida (1505-09) was the first Portuguese Governor and Viceroy in India; Albuquerque was the second.

s:
Consider the following fruits:
1. Papaya
2. Pineapple
3. Guava
How many of the above were introduced in India by the Portuguese in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries?
x: All three - papaya, pineapple and guava - are American fruits brought to India by the Portuguese in the 16th-17th centuries.

s: The cotton clothes of Calicut, which were taken by the Portuguese, were commonly called in Europe as
x: Cotton cloth exported from Calicut was called 'calico' in Europe, after the port's name.

s: Which one of the following crops was introduced by the Portuguese in India?
x: Chilli is an American crop brought to India by the Portuguese; opium, coffee and betel leaf are not Portuguese introductions.

s: Which Fruit was introduced by the Portuguese to the Telugu soil?
x: The tomato, an American plant, came to the Telugu country with the Portuguese; banana, apple and orange were known in India long before.

s:
With reference to St. Francis Xavier, consider the following statements:

1. St. Francis Xavier was one of the founding members of the Jesuit Order

2. St. Francis Xavier died in Goa and a church is dedicated to him there

3. The feast of St. Francis Xavier is celebrated in Goa each year
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: 1 and 3 only. St. Francis Xavier was a founding member of the Jesuits (1534), and his feast is celebrated in Goa every 3 December. He died on Shangchuan island off China (1552), not in Goa, though his body lies in the Basilica of Bom Jesus.

s: In India, Tobacco crop was first introduced by
x: The Portuguese brought tobacco to India, along with chilli, potato, pineapple and groundnut. (Moved to the Portuguese row.)

s: At which one of the following places in India did the Portuguese build their first fortress?
x: The first Portuguese fortress in India was built at Cochin in 1503; Cannanore and Anjediva followed in 1505 and Goa was taken in 1510.

s: The ruler of Gujarat Bahadur Shah was killed in conflict with
x: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat was killed by the Portuguese in 1537: invited aboard a Portuguese ship during negotiations, he was killed.

s: Krishnadeva Raya had friendly relation with whom among the given options?
x: Krishnadeva Raya kept friendly relations with the Portuguese: he traded horses through them, let Albuquerque build a fort at Bhatkal and helped at Goa.

s: Where did the Portuguese construct their first fort in India?
x: The first Portuguese fort in India was at Cochin (1503); Anjediva and Cannanore (1505) and Goa (1510) came later. 'Coonoor' here is a misprint for Cannanore.

s: Hooghly was used as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal by :
x: The Portuguese used Hooghly as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal, until Shah Jahan's governor Qasim Khan took it in 1632.

s: Who used Hooghly as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal?
x: The Portuguese used Hooghly as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal, until Shah Jahan's governor Qasim Khan took it in 1632.

s: Which part of India remained under Portuguese control after 15th August, 1947?
x: Goa (with Daman and Diu) stayed under Portuguese control after 15 August 1947 until Operation Vijay, 19 December 1961.

s: Against which colonial power did the freedom struggle have to continue in India even after 15 August, 1947?
x: After 15 August 1947 the struggle went on against the Portuguese in Goa, Daman and Diu, freed only in 1961 (Operation Vijay).

s: The Naval Trade License introduced by the Portuguese in India was called:
x: The Portuguese naval trade licence was the cartaz: Asian ships had to buy a pass, or be confiscated. The other options are not historical systems.

s: After coming to India, where did the Dutch establish their first factory in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Dutch set up their first factory in Andhra (and India) at Masulipatnam in 1605, with Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's permission; Nizampatnam (1606) and Pulicat (1610) came later.

s: What was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's establishments in India?
x: Nagapattinam (taken from the Portuguese in 1658) was the headquarters of the Dutch in India from 1690; before that the Coromandel HQ was Pulicat. Masulipatnam ('Musula') was their first factory.

s: Where was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's settlements in India?
x: Nagapattinam (taken from the Portuguese in 1658) was the headquarters of the Dutch in India from 1690; before that the Coromandel HQ was Pulicat. Masulipatnam ('Musula') was their first factory.

s: In which year did the Dutch establish their first factory at Pulicat, which was later abandoned?
x: The Dutch factory at Pulicat dates from 1610 (some books 1609), their second after Masulipatnam.

s: Which was the capital of Dutch settlement in Andhra?
x: Pulicat was the Dutch headquarters (capital) on the Coromandel coast till 1690, then Nagapattinam; Kalingapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada were not.

s: Where was the Governor of the Dutch Company based till 1689?
x: The Dutch Governor of the Coromandel was based at Pulicat till 1689-90, after which Nagapattinam became the HQ; Pondicherry was French and Madras English.

s: Where did the Dutch found their first factory in India?
x: The Dutch founded their first factory at Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) in Andhra in 1605; Pulicat (1609-10), Surat (1616) and Bheemunipatnam (1641) came later.

s: At which place in Andhra did the Dutch East India Company set up its first factory?
x: The Dutch founded their first factory at Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) in Andhra in 1605; Pulicat (1609-10), Surat (1616) and Bheemunipatnam (1641) came later.

s: In India, among the following locations, the Dutch established their earliest factory at
x: Of the options the earliest Dutch factory was Pulicat (1609); Surat was 1616, and Cochin (1663) and Cassimbazar later. Their very first factory, Masulipatnam (1605), is not offered.

s: The United East-India Company of the Netherlands first established its factories in this Andhra Area
x: The Dutch founded their first factory at Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) in Andhra in 1605; Pulicat (1609-10), Surat (1616) and Bheemunipatnam (1641) came later.

s: In which of the following places the Dutch established their trading centre in India?
x: All the above: the Dutch traded at Nagapattinam, Chinsura and Machilipatnam, at Surat, Broach and Agra, and at Cochin, Ahmedabad and Patna.

s: Which of the following regions was a Dutch colony?
x: Bheemili (Bheemunipatnam, 1641) was Dutch. Yanam and Mahe were French, and Karaikal, briefly Dutch (1645), was French from 1739.

s: Which of the following factories of Bengal was established by the Dutch?
x: Chinsurah (near Hooghly) was the Dutch factory in Bengal (Fort Gustavus); Bandel and Hooghly were Portuguese, Serampore Danish.

s: Dutch East India Company established its factory at Patna in which year?
x: The Dutch factory at Patna dates from 1632 (the BPSC key; some histories give 1638).

s: Which place is famously known as ‘Dutch Palace’?
x: Mattancherry Palace in Kochi, built by the Portuguese (c. 1555) for the Raja of Cochin and renovated by the Dutch, is called the Dutch Palace.

s: Which one of the following is the correct statement?
o: The modern Kochi was a Dutch colony till India’s Independence.
The Dutch defeated the Portuguese and built Fort Williams in the modern Kochi.
The modern Kochi was first a Dutch colony before the Portuguese took over from them.
The modern Kochi never became a part of the British colony.
x: The Dutch took Kochi from the Portuguese in 1663 and rebuilt the fort (Fort Williams); Kochi was Portuguese first, passed to the British (1795/1814) and was not Dutch at Independence.

s: Why did Dutch East India Company fail to maintain its influence in India ?
o: Portuguese did not allow them to trade in India.
There was a growing interference of Dutch Government in the Company’s internal affairs.
Dutch indulged in forcible religious conversion of the people and thus were expelled by local kings.
The English forces made them to leave India.
x: The English drove the Dutch out: the long rivalry, the 1667 compromise and the defeat at Bedara/Hooghly (1759) ended Dutch influence in India, and their real interest lay in the Indonesian spice islands.

s: Who was the Mughal Emperor, who issued farman to East India Company to start a factory at Surat?

x: The first English factories – Masulipatnam (1611, temporary) and Surat (1613, permanent) – were set up in Jahangir's reign.

s: Jahangir's Court was visited by the English trader, namely:

s: With whose permission did the English set up their first factory in Surat?

s: In the year 1613, where was the English East India Company given permission to set up a factory (trading post)?
x: Surat got the first permanent English factory in 1613 through Jahangir's farman. Masulipatnam (1611) was earlier but only temporary.

s: Where was the Western Presidency situated in the early period of the East India Company?
x: Surat was the seat of the Company's Western Presidency until it was moved to Bombay in 1687.

s: Where was the Western presidency situated is the early period of the East India company?
x: Surat was the early Western Presidency of the Company and was later replaced by Bombay (1687).

s: The first factory of the East India Company was established at –
x: Surat (1613) was the Company's first permanent factory in India. The other options were never EIC first factories, and Machilipatnam (1611) was only temporary.

s: The English established their first factory in India at
x: The English first set up a permanent factory at Surat in 1613. Bombay, Madras and Sutanuti (Calcutta) came later.

s:
In the first quarter of the seventeenth century, in which of the following was/were the factory/factories of the English East India Company located?

2. Chicacole
3. Trichinopoly
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Roe's privileges (1615-19) included a factory at Broach; Chicacole and Trichinopoly had no English factory in the first quarter of the 17th century. UPSC key: 1 only.

s: The Charter of 1600 issued by the British Queen bestowed the following on the East India Company
o: The powers of territorial governance of India
Unlimited powers to make civil and criminal legislation in India
To Act as agent of Crown in all dealings with all the Indian Kingdoms
Exclusive trading rights in the regions of America, Africa and Asia
x: The Charter of 1600 gave only exclusive (monopoly) trading rights east of the Cape of Good Hope up to the Straits of Magellan for 15 years; it gave no territorial governance, legislative power or agency of the Crown.

s: In which year was the English East India Company established?
x: Queen Elizabeth I chartered the English East India Company on 31 December 1600.

s: Which one of the following was the Emperor of India when the British East India Company was formed in London?
x: The Company was formed by the charter of 31 December 1600, when Akbar (1556-1605) ruled India.

s: Who was the ruler of India when the English East India Company was formed?
x: The English East India Company was formed in 1600, during Akbar's reign (1556-1605); Jahangir came in 1605.

s: The secret of success of East India Company in India was :
o: The company army received western training and they
Indian Soldiers lacked fidelity consequently the one
x: The book answer counts all three factors – absence of nationalism, a western-trained army and the lack of loyalty among Indian soldiers – as reasons for the Company's success.

s: Which of the following British companies got the first charter permitting them to trade in India?
o: The English Company trading to the East Indies
x: The East India Company got the royal charter of 31 December 1600 to trade with the East Indies. The Levant Company traded with the Ottoman lands, and 'The English Company trading to the East Indies' was the rival company of 1698.

s: Indian ruler, contemporary of Queen Elizabeth-I of England, was

s: Name the first English Voyage to come in India.
x: The Company's first voyage (1601-02) under James Lancaster sailed in the flagship Red Dragon and set up a factory at Bantam; the Mayflower carried the Pilgrims to America.

s: When was the British East India Company established in India?

src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(B) VRO / Village Surv
s: The first English settlement in India to be fortified was
x: Fort St. George, Madras (1639-44), was the first fortified English settlement and the first fort built by the English in India; Fort William came in 1700, and Mahim and Aguada were not English forts.

s: The place of English East India Company settlement in Madras was known as

x: The English settlements in Andhra and Fort St. George were trading posts dealing mainly in locally woven piece-goods (chintz, calico), not conquest, spices or agriculture.

s: The first English factory in Bengal was
x: Hugli (1651), on Shah Shuja's permission, was the first English factory in Bengal; Calcutta came only in 1690. Hariharpur and Balasore (1633) are in Odisha.

s: Who founded the Fort William George (Calcutta)?

s: At which place in Bengal did the Mughal Emperor grant the permission to East India Company to trade and set up its factories in 1651?

s: Who among the following was the founder of Calcutta?

s: Who founded Calcutta?

s: What is the name of the fort constructed by British in Calcutta?
x: The fortified English settlement at Calcutta was named Fort William in 1700. Fort St. David is at Cuddalore.

s: Identify the region from where Europeans got best shora (Saltpetre) and opium –
x: Saltpetre (shora) and opium came mainly from Bihar.
